symbols.name: \operatorname{pa}_{G}(v)
symbols.def: The vertices with a directed edge into \(v\) in \(G\).

symbols.name: \operatorname{bi}_{G}(v)
symbols.def: The bidirected edges of \(G\) incident to \(v\).

symbols.name: \mathcal S_G
symbols.def: \(\mathcal S_G=V\mathbin{\dot\cup}E^{\leftrightarrow}(G)\), with one private source per vertex and one source per bidirected edge.

symbols.name: \mathcal M'
symbols.def: A second model on the same \(G\) and \(\mathcal A\) as \(\mathcal M\).

symbols.name: \mathfrak I_{\mathrm{MIC}}(G,\mathcal A)
symbols.type: normalized marginally informationally complete menu class

symbols.name: \mathcal I_q
symbols.def: \(\mathcal I_q=\{(\rho,\boldsymbol b):\rho\in\mathcal R,\ \boldsymbol b\in\prod_{v\in V}\mathcal B_{v,j_v}\}\).

symbols.name: \mathcal E_{\mathcal I}
symbols.sig: \(\mathcal E_{\mathcal I}(\mathcal M)=(q_{\rho}(\boldsymbol b))_{(\rho,\boldsymbol b)\in\mathcal I_q}\)

symbols.name: G_{\mathrm b}
symbols.def: The graph on \(\{X_{\mathrm b},Y_{\mathrm b}\}\) with \(X_{\mathrm b}\to Y_{\mathrm b}\) and \(X_{\mathrm b}\leftrightarrow Y_{\mathrm b}\).

symbols.name: A_{\mathrm b}
symbols.space: A real matrix with rows \(\beta_X\in\mathcal L_{X_{\mathrm b}}\) and columns \((a_{\mathrm b},z_{\mathrm b})\in\mathcal A_{X_{\mathrm b}}^2\).

symbols.name: B_{\mathcal M,y}
symbols.def: \(B_{\mathcal M,y}(a_{\mathrm b},z_{\mathrm b})=W_{\mathcal M}((a_{\mathrm b},y)\mid(z_{\mathrm b},y))\).

symbols.name: h
symbols.space: \(h\in\ker(A_{\mathrm b})\) with \(r_{z^{\circ}}^{\mathsf T}h\ne0\), chosen when \(r_{z^{\circ}}\notin\operatorname{row}(A_{\mathrm b})\).

symbols.name: T
symbols.space: \(T\in\mathbb R^{\mathcal A_{X_{\mathrm b}}^2\times(\mathcal A_{X_{\mathrm b}}\times\mathcal A_{X_{\mathrm b}})}\cong\mathbb R^{m^2\times m^2}\).
symbols.def: \(T[(a_{\mathrm b},z_{\mathrm b}),(u_{\mathrm b},z'_{\mathrm b})]=\mathbf 1\{z_{\mathrm b}=z'_{\mathrm b}\}\bigl(\mathbf 1\{a_{\mathrm b}=u_{\mathrm b}\}/(2m)+1/(2m^2)\bigr)\).

symbols.name: g
symbols.space: \(g\in\mathbb R^{\mathcal A_{X_{\mathrm b}}\times\mathcal A_{X_{\mathrm b}}}\), indexed by \((u_{\mathrm b},z_{\mathrm b})\).
symbols.def: \(g(u_{\mathrm b},z_{\mathrm b})=2m h(u_{\mathrm b},z_{\mathrm b})-\sum_{a_{\mathrm b}\in\mathcal A_{X_{\mathrm b}}}h(a_{\mathrm b},z_{\mathrm b})\), the coordinate formula for \(T^{-1}h\).

symbols.name: B_y^{\sigma}
symbols.sig: \(B_y^{\sigma}(a_{\mathrm b},z_{\mathrm b})=\sum_{u_{\mathrm b}}m^{-1}f_{X_{\mathrm b}}(a_{\mathrm b}\mid u_{\mathrm b})f_{Y_{\mathrm b}}^{\sigma}(y\mid z_{\mathrm b},u_{\mathrm b})\)

symbols.name: G_{\mathrm f}
symbols.def: The graph has \(X_{\mathrm f}\to M_{\mathrm f}\to Y_{\mathrm f}\) and \(X_{\mathrm f}\leftrightarrow Y_{\mathrm f}\).

symbols.name: \mathcal C

definitions.name: \mathfrak M_{\mathrm{pp}}^{\mathrm{edge}}(G,\mathcal A)
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{pp}}^{\mathrm{edge}}(G,\mathcal A)=\{\mathcal M=((p_s)_{s\in\mathcal S_G},(f_v)_{v\in V}):p_{\mathcal M}^{U}(u)=\prod_{s\in\mathcal S_G}p_s(u_s),\ p_s(u_s)>0,\ f_v(a_v\mid z_{\operatorname{pa}_G(v)},u_v,u_{\operatorname{bi}_G(v)})>0\text{ for every admissible cell}\}\).

definitions.name: \mathfrak I_{\mathrm{MIC}}(G,\mathcal A)
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak I_{\mathrm{MIC}}(G,\mathcal A)=\{\mathcal I:\sum_{b_v\in\mathcal B_{v,j_v}}\phi_{v,(j_v,b_v)}(a_v)=1\text{ for every }(v,j_v,a_v),\ \operatorname{span}\{\phi_{v,\beta_v}:\beta_v\in\mathcal L_v\}=\mathbb R^{\mathcal A_v},\ \operatorname{span}\{\psi_{v,\beta_v}:\beta_v\in\mathcal L_v\}=\mathbb R^{\mathcal A_v}\text{ for every }v\in V\}\).

definitions.name: W_{\mathcal M}
definitions.construction: \(W_{\mathcal M}(a\mid z)=\sum_{u\in\prod_{s\in\mathcal S_G}\mathcal U_s}\prod_{s\in\mathcal S_G}p_s(u_s)\prod_{v\in V}f_v(a_v\mid z_{\operatorname{pa}_G(v)},u_v,u_{\operatorname{bi}_G(v)})\).

definitions.name: \mathcal E_{\mathcal I}
definitions.construction: \(q_{\rho}(\boldsymbol b)=\sum_{a,z}W_{\mathcal M}(a\mid z)\prod_{v\in V}\phi_{v,(j_v,b_v)}(a_v)\psi_{v,(j_v,b_v)}(z_v)\), and \(\mathcal E_{\mathcal I}(\mathcal M)=(q_{\rho}(\boldsymbol b))_{(\rho,\boldsymbol b)\in\mathcal I_q}\).

definitions.name: Q_{x,y}(\mathcal M)
definitions.construction: \(Q_{x,y}(\mathcal M)=\sum_{a,z}W_{\mathcal M}(a\mid z)\mathbf 1\{a_Y=y\}\prod_{v\in X}\mathbf 1\{z_v=x_v\}\prod_{v\notin X}\mathbf 1\{z_v=a_v\}\).

definitions.name: \mathcal Q_{\mathcal I}
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal Q_{\mathcal I}=\{\mathcal E_{\mathcal I}(\mathcal M):\mathcal M\in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{pp}}^{\mathrm{edge}}(G,\mathcal A)\}\).

definitions.name: \Theta_{x,y}(q)
definitions.construction: \(\Theta_{x,y}(q)=\{Q_{x,y}(\mathcal M):\mathcal M\in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{pp}}^{\mathrm{edge}}(G,\mathcal A),\ \mathcal E_{\mathcal I}(\mathcal M)=q\}\).

definitions.name: \operatorname{GID}_{\mathcal I}(Q_{x,y})
definitions.construction: \(\operatorname{GID}_{\mathcal I}(Q_{x,y})\Longleftrightarrow[\mathcal E_{\mathcal I}(\mathcal M)=\mathcal E_{\mathcal I}(\mathcal M')\Rightarrow Q_{x,y}(\mathcal M)=Q_{x,y}(\mathcal M')]\) for every \(\mathcal M,\mathcal M'\in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{pp}}^{\mathrm{edge}}(G,\mathcal A)\).

definitions.name: \mu^y
definitions.construction: Whenever \(e_y\in\operatorname{span}\{\phi_{Y_{\mathrm b},\beta_Y}:\beta_Y\in\mathcal L_{Y_{\mathrm b}}\}\), choose \(\mu^y\in\mathbb R^{\mathcal L_{Y_{\mathrm b}}}\) satisfying \(\sum_{\beta_Y\in\mathcal L_{Y_{\mathrm b}}}\mu^y_{\beta_Y}\phi_{Y_{\mathrm b},\beta_Y}(a_{\mathrm t})=e_y(a_{\mathrm t})=\mathbf 1\{a_{\mathrm t}=y\}\) for every \(a_{\mathrm t}\in\mathcal A_{Y_{\mathrm b}}\); a second admissible choice \(\widetilde\mu^y\) satisfies the same coordinate equations.

definitions.name: q^{\mathrm b}_{\beta_X}(y;\mu^y)
definitions.construction: \(q^{\mathrm b}_{\beta_X}(y;\mu^y)=\sum_{\beta_Y\in\mathcal L_{Y_{\mathrm b}}}\mu^y_{\beta_Y}\bar q_{\beta_X,\beta_Y}\), where \(\bar q_{\beta_X,\beta_Y}=q_{(j_X,j_Y)}(b_X,b_Y)\) for \(\beta_X=(j_X,b_X)\) and \(\beta_Y=(j_Y,b_Y)\).

definitions.name: A_{\mathrm b}
definitions.construction: \(A_{\mathrm b}[\beta_X,(a_{\mathrm b},z_{\mathrm b})]=\phi_{X_{\mathrm b},\beta_X}(a_{\mathrm b})\psi_{X_{\mathrm b},\beta_X}(z_{\mathrm b})\) for \(\beta_X\in\mathcal L_{X_{\mathrm b}}\) and \((a_{\mathrm b},z_{\mathrm b})\in\mathcal A_{X_{\mathrm b}}^2\).

definitions.name: r_{z^{\circ}}
definitions.construction: \(r_{z^{\circ}}[a_{\mathrm b},z_{\mathrm b}]=\mathbf 1\{z_{\mathrm b}=z^{\circ}\}\) for \((a_{\mathrm b},z_{\mathrm b})\in\mathcal A_{X_{\mathrm b}}^2\).

definitions.name: (\mathcal M_h^{+},\mathcal M_h^{-})
definitions.construction: Choose \(h\in\ker(A_{\mathrm b})\) with \(r_{z^{\circ}}^{\mathsf T}h\ne0\), identify the shared-edge alphabet with \(\mathcal A_{X_{\mathrm b}}\), and set \(p(u_{\mathrm b})=1/m\). Give all private sources one state. In both models set \(f_{X_{\mathrm b}}(a_{\mathrm b}\mid u_{\mathrm b})=\mathbf 1\{a_{\mathrm b}=u_{\mathrm b}\}/2+1/(2m)\). With \(T[(a_{\mathrm b},z_{\mathrm b}),(u_{\mathrm b},z'_{\mathrm b})]=\mathbf 1\{z_{\mathrm b}=z'_{\mathrm b}\}(\mathbf 1\{a_{\mathrm b}=u_{\mathrm b}\}/(2m)+1/(2m^2))\), set \(g(u_{\mathrm b},z_{\mathrm b})=2m h(u_{\mathrm b},z_{\mathrm b})-\sum_{a_{\mathrm b}}h(a_{\mathrm b},z_{\mathrm b})\), \(L=\lVert g\rVert_{\infty}\), and \(t=1/(2kL)\). Choose \(y^{\dagger}\ne y\). For \(\sigma\in\{+1,-1\}\), define \(f^{\sigma}_{Y_{\mathrm b}}(\ell\mid z_{\mathrm b},u_{\mathrm b})=1/k+\sigma t g(u_{\mathrm b},z_{\mathrm b})\) when \(\ell=y\), \(1/k-\sigma t g(u_{\mathrm b},z_{\mathrm b})\) when \(\ell=y^{\dagger}\), and \(1/k\) otherwise; \(\mathcal M_h^{\sigma}\) is the bow SCM with these source masses and node kernels.

definitions.name: \mathcal I_{\mathrm b}^{\dagger}
definitions.construction: At \(X_{\mathrm b}\), use three instruments: a one-branch instrument \((\phi,\psi)=(\mathbf 1,\psi^{+})\), a one-branch instrument \((\mathbf 1,\psi^{-})\), and a two-branch instrument \((e_0,\psi^{+}),(e_1,\psi^{+})\). At \(Y_{\mathrm b}\), use the two-branch instrument \((e_0,e_0),(e_1,e_1)\). Thus \(A_{\mathrm b}^{\dagger}\) has rows \(\mathbf 1\otimes\psi^{+},\mathbf 1\otimes\psi^{-},e_0\otimes\psi^{+},e_1\otimes\psi^{+}\).

definitions.name: (G_{\mathrm f},K_{\mathrm f},q_{\mathrm f},P_{\mathrm f})
definitions.construction: Use \(G_{\mathrm f}\), \(K_{\mathrm f}=\begin{pmatrix}3/4&1/4\\1/4&3/4\end{pmatrix}\), and \((q_{\mathrm f}(x_{\mathrm f},y_{\mathrm f},0),q_{\mathrm f}(x_{\mathrm f},y_{\mathrm f},1))=(33,15),(7,9),(9,7),(15,33)\) divided by \(128\), in \((x_{\mathrm f},y_{\mathrm f})=(0,0),(0,1),(1,0),(1,1)\) order. Define each pair \((P_{\mathrm f}(x_{\mathrm f},y_{\mathrm f},0),P_{\mathrm f}(x_{\mathrm f},y_{\mathrm f},1))\) by left multiplication with \((K_{\mathrm f}^{\mathsf T})^{-1}\).

definitions.name: R_{\mathcal C}
definitions.construction: Fix every coefficient \(R_{\mathcal C}[\eta,i]\in\mathbb R\), for \(\eta\in\mathcal I_{\mathcal C}\) and \(i\in\mathcal I_q\), and set \(k_{\mathcal C}(q)_\eta=\sum_{i\in\mathcal I_q}R_{\mathcal C}[\eta,i]q_i\).

definitions.name: (U_w,V_w)
definitions.construction: For \(\eta=(a_D,a_w,a_H)\in\mathcal I_{\mathcal C}\), set \(U_w[(a_w,a_{\operatorname{mb}_{\mathcal C}(w)},a_H),\eta]=\mathbf 1\{\eta\text{ agrees on }(a_w,a_{\operatorname{mb}_{\mathcal C}(w)},a_H)\}\) and \(V_w[(a_{\operatorname{mb}_{\mathcal C}(w)},a_H),\eta]=\mathbf 1\{\eta\text{ agrees on }(a_{\operatorname{mb}_{\mathcal C}(w)},a_H)\}\). Matrix multiplication therefore performs exactly the two displayed marginalizations.

definitions.name: \Phi_w
definitions.construction: For \(\xi=(a_D,a_H,a_w)\in\mathcal I_D\), \(\eta=(a_D,a_w,a_H)\), and \(h=(a_{\operatorname{mb}_{\mathcal C}(w)},a_H)\), define \(\Phi_w(k_{\mathcal C})_\xi=k_{\mathcal C,\eta}(V_wk_{\mathcal C})_h/(U_wk_{\mathcal C})_{(a_w,h)}\).

definitions.name: (N_D,O_D,S_D)
definitions.construction: Set \(N_D[(a_H,a_w),(a_D',a_H',a_w')]=\mathbf 1\{(a_H,a_w)=(a_H',a_w')\}\). Fix a finite explicit list \(\Omega_D\) of retained overlap rows; for each \(r\in\Omega_D\), record its stated district-cell coefficients as \(O_D[r,\xi]\) and its stated accessible-coordinate coefficients as \(S_D[r,i]\), so the complete retained contract is the coordinate equality \(\sum_{\xi\in\mathcal I_D}O_D[r,\xi]\kappa_D(\xi)=\sum_{i\in\mathcal I_q}S_D[r,i]q_i\) for every \(r\in\Omega_D\).

definitions.name: \mathcal K_D^{\mathrm{alg}}(q^{\star})
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal K_D^{\mathrm{alg}}(q^{\star})=\{\kappa_D\in\mathbb R^{\mathcal I_D}:k_{\mathcal C}(q^{\star})>0,\ U_wk_{\mathcal C}(q^{\star})>0,\ \kappa_D=\Phi_w(k_{\mathcal C}(q^{\star}))>0,\ N_D\kappa_D=\mathbf 1,\ O_D\kappa_D=S_Dq^{\star}\}\).

definitions.name: \mathsf H_{\mathrm{lift}}
definitions.construction: Apply source splitting to the positive table \(k_{\mathcal C}(q^{\star})\), formulate the required private-source and per-bidirected-edge masses as a product-constrained transportation polytope, and seek a rational interior point whose contractions are \(q^{\star}\) and whose coordinate fixing image is \(\kappa_D\), while holding every observed-node table \(f_v\) common across the two models.

statements.statement: For every \(\mathcal M\in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{pp}}^{\mathrm{edge}}(G,\mathcal A)\) and normalized separable menu \(\mathcal I\), every accessible branch law equals its coordinate in \(\mathcal E_{\mathcal I}(\mathcal M)\), and every atomic intervention query equals the displayed contraction of the same \(W_{\mathcal M}\).
statements.justification: The reduction supplies a single finite tensor on which both the probe coordinates and the intervention target are linear contractions.
statements.gap: Friend et al. use local process contractions for Markovian models; this lemma fixes the independent edge-source ADMG semantics needed for the bow and one-step contracts.
statements.consumer: Every bow oracle and the Ananke coordinate backend use this common tensor interface.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(\mathcal M\in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{pp}}^{\mathrm{edge}}(G,\mathcal A)\), a regime \(\rho=(j_v:v\in V)\), and a branch vector \(\boldsymbol b=(b_v:v\in V)\).  By \texttt{ass:independent-sources}, conditional on the source configuration \(u\), the structural part of the finite generative mass is
\[
 \prod_{s\in\mathcal S_G}p_s(u_s)
 \prod_{v\in V}f_v\!\left(a_v\mid
 z_{\operatorname{pa}_G(v)},u_v,u_{\operatorname{bi}_G(v)}\right).
\]
For the selected local branch \(\beta_v=(j_v,b_v)\), the separable kernel contributes
\[
 K_{v,\beta_v}(z_v,a_v)
 =\psi_{v,\beta_v}(z_v)\phi_{v,\beta_v}(a_v).
\]
Therefore finite marginalization over \(u,a,z\) gives the branch probability
\[
\begin{aligned}
 P_{\mathcal M,\rho}(\boldsymbol b)
 &=\sum_{u,a,z}
 \prod_{s\in\mathcal S_G}p_s(u_s)
 \prod_{v\in V}
 f_v\!\left(a_v\mid z_{\operatorname{pa}_G(v)},u_v,
 u_{\operatorname{bi}_G(v)}\right)
 \phi_{v,(j_v,b_v)}(a_v)\psi_{v,(j_v,b_v)}(z_v)\\
 &=\sum_{a,z}W_{\mathcal M}(a\mid z)
 \prod_{v\in V}\phi_{v,(j_v,b_v)}(a_v)
 \psi_{v,(j_v,b_v)}(z_v)\\
 &=q_\rho(\boldsymbol b).
\end{aligned}
\]
The second equality is exactly \texttt{def:split-port-kernel}, and the third is \texttt{def:probe-evidence-map}.  These numbers form a probability law: eliminate vertices in reverse topological order.  When a current sink \(v\) is eliminated, \(z_v\) occurs in no remaining child mechanism, and
\[
 \sum_{a_v,b_v,z_v}f_v(a_v\mid\cdots)
 \phi_{v,(j_v,b_v)}(a_v)\psi_{v,(j_v,b_v)}(z_v)
 =\sum_{a_v}f_v(a_v\mid\cdots)
 \sum_{b_v}\phi_{v,(j_v,b_v)}(a_v)=1.
\]
Here \(\sum_{z_v}\psi_{v,(j_v,b_v)}(z_v)=1\) because each \(\psi_{v,\beta_v}\) is a probability state, \(\sum_{b_v}\phi_{v,(j_v,b_v)}(a_v)=1\) by \texttt{ass:instrument-normalization}, and each \(f_v\) is a stochastic kernel.  Acyclicity of \(G\) makes the elimination terminate, and the source masses then sum to one.

It remains to verify that the causal target is a contraction of the same tensor.  For \(a\in\prod_v\mathcal A_v\), define the split input \(z^{x}(a)\) by \(z^{x}_v(a)=x_v\) for \(v\in X\) and \(z^{x}_v(a)=a_v\) for \(v\notin X\).  Under \(\operatorname{do}(X=x)\), every kernel at a vertex in \(X\) is removed.  Equivalently, one may insert that normalized kernel and sum its otherwise unused structural output \(a_v\), because \(\sum_{a_v}f_v(a_v\mid\cdots)=1\), even when its source is shared with another vertex.  Thus
\[
\begin{aligned}
 P_{\mathcal M}(Y=y\mid\operatorname{do}(X=x))
 &=\sum_{u,a_{V\setminus X}}\mathbf 1\{a_Y=y\}
 \prod_s p_s(u_s)\prod_{v\notin X}
 f_v\!\left(a_v\mid z^x_{\operatorname{pa}_G(v)}(a),
 u_v,u_{\operatorname{bi}_G(v)}\right)\\
 &=\sum_a\mathbf 1\{a_Y=y\}
 W_{\mathcal M}\!\left(a\mid z^x(a)\right)\\
 &=\sum_{a,z}W_{\mathcal M}(a\mid z)\mathbf 1\{a_Y=y\}
 \prod_{v\in X}\mathbf 1\{z_v=x_v\}
 \prod_{v\notin X}\mathbf 1\{z_v=a_v\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
The last display is \texttt{def:atomic-query-contraction}.  Hence both every accessible branch law and the atomic intervention query are the asserted contractions of \(W_{\mathcal M}\).

statements.statement: For \(G_{\mathrm b}\) and a normalized separable menu, suppose \(e_y\in\operatorname{span}\{\phi_{Y_{\mathrm b},\beta_Y}:\beta_Y\in\mathcal L_{Y_{\mathrm b}}\}\). Every admissible \(\mu^y\) satisfies \(\sum_{\beta_Y}\mu^y_{\beta_Y}\phi_{Y_{\mathrm b},\beta_Y}(a_{\mathrm t})=\mathbf 1\{a_{\mathrm t}=y\}\). Because \(Y_{\mathrm b}\) is terminal and every \(\psi_{Y_{\mathrm b},\beta_Y}\) is normalized, for every attainable bow tensor, \(q^{\mathrm b}_{\beta_X}(y;\mu^y)=\sum_{a_{\mathrm b},z_{\mathrm b}}A_{\mathrm b}[\beta_X,(a_{\mathrm b},z_{\mathrm b})]B_{\mathcal M,y}(a_{\mathrm b},z_{\mathrm b})\) and \(Q_{z^{\circ},y}(\mathcal M)=\sum_{a_{\mathrm b},z_{\mathrm b}}r_{z^{\circ}}[a_{\mathrm b},z_{\mathrm b}]B_{\mathcal M,y}(a_{\mathrm b},z_{\mathrm b})\). If \(\mu^y\) and \(\widetilde\mu^y\) both satisfy the effect-synthesis equations, their responses coincide; the common coordinate is denoted \(q^{\mathrm b}_{\beta_X}(y)\).
statements.justification: Terminal recovery must be a property of the probe tensor, not of an arbitrary effect dual frame.
statements.gap: The terminal bow input is causally unused, so separate normalization of terminal probe states reduces recovery to the weaker marginal effect span; this lemma proves exact synthesis invariance for that reduction.
statements.consumer: Ananke may choose any numerically stable terminal effect dual without changing the synthesized response vector.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix a normalized separable menu on \(G_{\mathrm b}\), an attainable tensor generated by \(\mathcal M\), and \(y\in\mathcal A_{Y_{\mathrm b}}\) such that \(e_y\) belongs to the span of the terminal effect vectors.  By \texttt{def:terminal-synthesis}, an admissible \(\mu^y\) obeys, for every \(a_{\mathrm t}\in\mathcal A_{Y_{\mathrm b}}\),
\[
 \sum_{\beta_Y\in\mathcal L_{Y_{\mathrm b}}}
 \mu^y_{\beta_Y}\phi_{Y_{\mathrm b},\beta_Y}(a_{\mathrm t})
 =e_y(a_{\mathrm t})
 =\mathbf 1\{a_{\mathrm t}=y\}.
\]
This is the asserted pointwise effect synthesis.

The vertex \(Y_{\mathrm b}\) has no directed child in \(G_{\mathrm b}\).  Hence \(Y_{\mathrm b}\notin\operatorname{pa}_{G_{\mathrm b}}(v)\) for both vertices \(v\), and inspection of \texttt{def:split-port-kernel} shows that the terminal input coordinate is absent from every structural-kernel factor.  Thus
\[
 W_{\mathcal M}((a_{\mathrm b},a_{\mathrm t})\mid
 (z_{\mathrm b},z_{\mathrm t}))
 =W_{\mathcal M}((a_{\mathrm b},a_{\mathrm t})\mid
 (z_{\mathrm b},z'_{\mathrm t}))
\]
for all terminal inputs \(z_{\mathrm t},z'_{\mathrm t}\).  Denote this common value by \(\overline W_{\mathcal M}(a_{\mathrm b},a_{\mathrm t}\mid z_{\mathrm b})\).

By \texttt{lem:split-port-reduction} and \texttt{def:bow-probe-matrix}, every pair of tagged branches satisfies
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \bar q_{\beta_X,\beta_Y}
 ={}&\sum_{a_{\mathrm b},z_{\mathrm b},a_{\mathrm t},z_{\mathrm t}}
 \overline W_{\mathcal M}(a_{\mathrm b},a_{\mathrm t}\mid z_{\mathrm b})
 A_{\mathrm b}[\beta_X,(a_{\mathrm b},z_{\mathrm b})]\\
 &\hspace{31mm}\cdot
 \phi_{Y_{\mathrm b},\beta_Y}(a_{\mathrm t})
 \psi_{Y_{\mathrm b},\beta_Y}(z_{\mathrm t}).
\end{aligned}
\]
All alphabets are finite, so the order of summation may be exchanged.  Moreover, each \(\psi_{Y_{\mathrm b},\beta_Y}\) is a probability vector and therefore sums to one.  Using \texttt{def:terminally-synthesized-bow-response} and then the effect-synthesis equation gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 q^{\mathrm b}_{\beta_X}(y;\mu^y)
 & =\sum_{a_{\mathrm b},z_{\mathrm b},a_{\mathrm t}}
 \overline W_{\mathcal M}(a_{\mathrm b},a_{\mathrm t}\mid z_{\mathrm b})
 A_{\mathrm b}[\beta_X,(a_{\mathrm b},z_{\mathrm b})]
 \sum_{\beta_Y}\mu^y_{\beta_Y}
 \phi_{Y_{\mathrm b},\beta_Y}(a_{\mathrm t})
 \sum_{z_{\mathrm t}}\psi_{Y_{\mathrm b},\beta_Y}(z_{\mathrm t})\\
 & =\sum_{a_{\mathrm b},z_{\mathrm b},a_{\mathrm t}}
 \overline W_{\mathcal M}(a_{\mathrm b},a_{\mathrm t}\mid z_{\mathrm b})
 A_{\mathrm b}[\beta_X,(a_{\mathrm b},z_{\mathrm b})]
 \mathbf 1\{a_{\mathrm t}=y\}\\
 & =\sum_{a_{\mathrm b},z_{\mathrm b}}
 A_{\mathrm b}[\beta_X,(a_{\mathrm b},z_{\mathrm b})]
 W_{\mathcal M}((a_{\mathrm b},y)\mid(z_{\mathrm b},y))\\
 & =\sum_{a_{\mathrm b},z_{\mathrm b}}
 A_{\mathrm b}[\beta_X,(a_{\mathrm b},z_{\mathrm b})]
 B_{\mathcal M,y}(a_{\mathrm b},z_{\mathrm b}).
\end{aligned}
\]
The apparently branch-dependent state vectors have disappeared precisely because terminality made the kernel independent of \(z_{\mathrm t}\).

For the causal query, \texttt{def:atomic-query-contraction} sets \(z_{\mathrm b}=z^{\circ}\), sets the nonintervened terminal input equal to its output, and sets that output to \(y\).  Therefore, by \texttt{def:bow-target-coefficient},
\[
\begin{aligned}
 Q_{z^{\circ},y}(\mathcal M)
 &=\sum_{a_{\mathrm b}}
 W_{\mathcal M}((a_{\mathrm b},y)\mid(z^{\circ},y))\\
 &=\sum_{a_{\mathrm b},z_{\mathrm b}}
 r_{z^{\circ}}[a_{\mathrm b},z_{\mathrm b}]
 B_{\mathcal M,y}(a_{\mathrm b},z_{\mathrm b}).
\end{aligned}
\]
If \(\widetilde\mu^y\) is another solution of the effect-synthesis equations, the preceding calculation applies verbatim and gives the same vector \(A_{\mathrm b}B_{\mathcal M,y}\).  Hence
\[
 q^{\mathrm b}_{\beta_X}(y;\mu^y)
 =q^{\mathrm b}_{\beta_X}(y;\widetilde\mu^y)
\]
for every \(\beta_X\).  The common evidence-determined coordinate is therefore well defined as \(q^{\mathrm b}_{\beta_X}(y)\).

statements.statement: The operator \(T\) is an invertible \(m^2\)-by-\(m^2\) block-diagonal matrix, with one block \(I/(2m)+\mathbf 1\mathbf 1^{\mathsf T}/(2m^2)\) for each \(z_{\mathrm b}\), and its inverse block is \(2mI-\mathbf 1\mathbf 1^{\mathsf T}\). Therefore the explicit coordinate definition of \(g\) satisfies \(Tg=h\), so \(L>0\), and \(B_y^{+}-B_y^{-}=2th\). For every branch pair, \([\mathcal E_{\mathcal I}(\mathcal M_h^{+})]_{\beta_X,\beta_Y}-[\mathcal E_{\mathcal I}(\mathcal M_h^{-})]_{\beta_X,\beta_Y}=2t(A_{\mathrm b}h)_{\beta_X}[\phi_{Y_{\mathrm b},\beta_Y}(y)-\phi_{Y_{\mathrm b},\beta_Y}(y^{\dagger})]=0\), whereas \(Q_{z^{\circ},y}(\mathcal M_h^{+})-Q_{z^{\circ},y}(\mathcal M_h^{-})=2t r_{z^{\circ}}^{\mathsf T}h\ne0\).
statements.justification: This calculation makes the repaired dimensions and the exact evidence-null and query-separation identities auditable coordinate by coordinate.
statements.gap: Existing hedge constructions do not provide this typed \(m^2\)-coordinate disturbing-probe cancellation identity.
statements.consumer: Ananke can verify a failed bow certificate using two matrix products and the displayed nonzero scalar.
statements.proof_tex:
For a fixed input coordinate \(z_{\mathrm b}\), the corresponding block of \(T\) is
\[
 C=\frac{1}{2m}I+\frac{1}{2m^2}J,
 \qquad J=\mathbf 1\mathbf 1^{\mathsf T}.
\]
Since \(J^2=mJ\), direct multiplication gives
\[
 C(2mI-J)
 =I-\frac{1}{2m}J+\frac{1}{m}J-\frac{1}{2m}J=I,
\]
and the same computation in the reverse order gives \((2mI-J)C=I\).  Thus every block is invertible with inverse \(2mI-J\).  The Kronecker factor \(\mathbf 1\{z_{\mathrm b}=z'_{\mathrm b}\}\) in \texttt{def:bow-positive-twin-construction} makes \(T\) block diagonal with exactly \(m\) such blocks, so \(T\) is an invertible \(m^2\)-by-\(m^2\) matrix.

On the block indexed by \(z_{\mathrm b}\), the displayed definition of \(g\) is precisely
\[
 g(\,cdot\,,z_{\mathrm b})=(2mI-J)h(\,\cdot\,,z_{\mathrm b}).
\]
Consequently \(Tg=h\).  The condition \(r_{z^{\circ}}^{\mathsf T}h\ne0\) implies \(h\ne0\), and invertibility of \(T\) then implies \(g\ne0\).  Since the array is finite, \(L=\lVert g\rVert_\infty>0\), so \(t=1/(2kL)\) is well defined and positive.

For the distinguished outcome \(y\), the two outcome kernels differ by
\[
 f^+_{Y_{\mathrm b}}(y\mid z_{\mathrm b},u_{\mathrm b})
 -f^-_{Y_{\mathrm b}}(y\mid z_{\mathrm b},u_{\mathrm b})
 =2t g(u_{\mathrm b},z_{\mathrm b}).
\]
Using the uniform shared source and the common treatment kernel from \texttt{def:bow-positive-twin-construction}, the response-table difference is therefore
\[
\begin{aligned}
 B_y^+(a_{\mathrm b},z_{\mathrm b})-B_y^-(a_{\mathrm b},z_{\mathrm b})
 &=2t\sum_{u_{\mathrm b}}
 \left(\frac{\mathbf 1\{a_{\mathrm b}=u_{\mathrm b}\}}{2m}
 +\frac{1}{2m^2}\right)g(u_{\mathrm b},z_{\mathrm b})\\
 &=2t(Tg)(a_{\mathrm b},z_{\mathrm b})
 =2t h(a_{\mathrm b},z_{\mathrm b}).
\end{aligned}
\]
The response-table difference at \(y^{\dagger}\) is the negative of this array, and it is zero at every other outcome cell.

Expand an arbitrary branch-pair evidence coordinate using \texttt{def:probe-evidence-map}.  The bow outcome mechanism does not depend on the terminal output port \(z_{\mathrm t}\), and \(\sum_{z_{\mathrm t}}\psi_{Y_{\mathrm b},\beta_Y}(z_{\mathrm t})=1\).  Hence the preceding two nonzero outcome differences yield
\[
\begin{aligned}
 &[\mathcal E_{\mathcal I}(\mathcal M_h^+)]_{\beta_X,\beta_Y}
 -[\mathcal E_{\mathcal I}(\mathcal M_h^-)]_{\beta_X,\beta_Y}\\
 &\quad=2t\sum_{a_{\mathrm b},z_{\mathrm b}}
 \phi_{X_{\mathrm b},\beta_X}(a_{\mathrm b})
 \psi_{X_{\mathrm b},\beta_X}(z_{\mathrm b})h(a_{\mathrm b},z_{\mathrm b})
 \bigl[\phi_{Y_{\mathrm b},\beta_Y}(y)
 -\phi_{Y_{\mathrm b},\beta_Y}(y^{\dagger})\bigr]\\
 &\quad=2t(A_{\mathrm b}h)_{\beta_X}
 \bigl[\phi_{Y_{\mathrm b},\beta_Y}(y)
 -\phi_{Y_{\mathrm b},\beta_Y}(y^{\dagger})\bigr]=0,
\end{aligned}
\]
where \(A_{\mathrm b}h=0\) follows from \(h\in\ker(A_{\mathrm b})\).  Finally, \texttt{def:atomic-query-contraction} sums the \(y\)-response table over \(a_{\mathrm b}\) at \(z_{\mathrm b}=z^{\circ}\).  Therefore
\[
 Q_{z^{\circ},y}(\mathcal M_h^+)-Q_{z^{\circ},y}(\mathcal M_h^-)
 =2t\sum_{a_{\mathrm b}}h(a_{\mathrm b},z^{\circ})
 =2t r_{z^{\circ}}^{\mathsf T}h\ne0.
\]

statements.statement: In \(G_{\mathrm b}\), if \(r_{z^{\circ}}\notin\operatorname{row}(A_{\mathrm b})\), choose \(h\in\ker(A_{\mathrm b})\) with \(r_{z^{\circ}}^{\mathsf T}h\ne0\). The construction \((\mathcal M_h^{+},\mathcal M_h^{-})\) gives two members of \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{pp}}^{\mathrm{edge}}(G_{\mathrm b},\mathcal A)\) with identical \(\mathcal E_{\mathcal I}\), unequal \(Q_{z^{\circ},y}\), exactly \(m\) states for the shared edge source, and primitive cell floor at least \(1/(2\max\{m,k\})\).
statements.justification: The failure witness is an interior pair of legal edge-source SCMs, not a signed array outside the causal model.
statements.gap: Shpitser and Pearl give passive-law hedge twins, while Kivva et al. treat observed-law positivity; neither construction preserves arbitrary disturbing-probe contractions under primitive positivity.
statements.consumer: This pair is Ananke's exact negative certificate for every failed bow row-span test.
statements.proof_tex:
Assume \(r_{z^{\circ}}\notin\operatorname{row}(A_{\mathrm b})\), and take the stipulated \(h\in\ker(A_{\mathrm b})\) with \(r_{z^{\circ}}^{\mathsf T}h\ne0\).  By \texttt{lem:bow-twin-coordinate-sanity}, \(L>0\), so every object in \texttt{def:bow-positive-twin-construction} is well defined.

The shared edge source has exactly \(m\) states, each of mass \(1/m>0\); every private source has one state of mass one.  For each \(u_{\mathrm b}\), the treatment kernel is normalized because
\[
 \sum_{a_{\mathrm b}}
 \left(\frac12\mathbf 1\{a_{\mathrm b}=u_{\mathrm b}\}
 +\frac{1}{2m}\right)=\frac12+\frac12=1,
\]
and every one of its cells is at least \(1/(2m)>0\).  For the outcome kernel, the perturbations at \(y\) and \(y^{\dagger}\) cancel, so its \(k\) cells sum to one.  Moreover,
\[
 |t g(u_{\mathrm b},z_{\mathrm b})|
 \le tL=\frac{1}{2k}.
\]
Thus each modified outcome cell is at least \(1/k-1/(2k)=1/(2k)>0\), and every unmodified cell is \(1/k\).  It follows from \texttt{ass:independent-sources}, \texttt{ass:strict-source-positivity}, \texttt{ass:strict-mechanism-positivity}, and \texttt{def:primitive-positive-edge-scm-class} that both \(\mathcal M_h^+\) and \(\mathcal M_h^-\) lie in \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{pp}}^{\mathrm{edge}}(G_{\mathrm b},\mathcal A)\).

The lower bounds just obtained also give a common primitive-cell floor.  Indeed,
\[
 \min\left\{1,\frac1m,\frac{1}{2m},\frac{1}{2k}\right\}
 =\frac{1}{2\max\{m,k\}}.
\]
Finally, \texttt{lem:bow-twin-coordinate-sanity} proves coordinate by coordinate that all branch-pair evidence differences vanish, while
\[
 Q_{z^{\circ},y}(\mathcal M_h^+)-Q_{z^{\circ},y}(\mathcal M_h^-)
 =2t r_{z^{\circ}}^{\mathsf T}h\ne0.
\]
Hence the two legal same-observed-alphabet models have identical \(\mathcal E_{\mathcal I}\), unequal targets, the asserted source-cardinality bound, and the asserted positive floor.

statements.statement: For an attainable bow tensor, if \(c^{\mathsf T}A_{\mathrm b}=\widetilde c^{\mathsf T}A_{\mathrm b}=r_{z^{\circ}}^{\mathsf T}\), then \(\sum_{\beta_X\in\mathcal L_{X_{\mathrm b}}}c_{\beta_X}q^{\mathrm b}_{\beta_X}(y)=\sum_{\beta_X\in\mathcal L_{X_{\mathrm b}}}\widetilde c_{\beta_X}q^{\mathrm b}_{\beta_X}(y)\).
statements.justification: The bow functional must not depend on which treatment-side row-span coefficients are selected.
statements.gap: Standard frame reconstruction gives coefficient invariance for full tomography; this lemma proves it only for the query-relevant bow row space.
statements.consumer: Ananke can change linear solvers or generalized inverses without changing the returned causal value.
statements.proof_tex:
For the attainable bow tensor, define \(b_y\in\mathbb R^{m^2}\) by
\[
 b_y[a_{\mathrm b},z_{\mathrm b}]=B_{\mathcal M,y}(a_{\mathrm b},z_{\mathrm b}).
\]
By \texttt{lem:terminal-synthesis-invariance}, the synthesis-invariant response vector satisfies
\[
 \bigl(q^{\mathrm b}_{\beta_X}(y):\beta_X\in\mathcal L_{X_{\mathrm b}}\bigr)
 =A_{\mathrm b}b_y.
\]
If \(c^{\mathsf T}A_{\mathrm b}=\widetilde c^{\mathsf T}A_{\mathrm b}=r_{z^{\circ}}^{\mathsf T}\), associativity of finite matrix multiplication yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \sum_{\beta_X}c_{\beta_X}q^{\mathrm b}_{\beta_X}(y)
 &=c^{\mathsf T}A_{\mathrm b}b_y
 =r_{z^{\circ}}^{\mathsf T}b_y\\
 &=\widetilde c^{\mathsf T}A_{\mathrm b}b_y
 =\sum_{\beta_X}\widetilde c_{\beta_X}q^{\mathrm b}_{\beta_X}(y).
\end{aligned}
\]
This proves coefficient invariance without requiring full column rank of \(A_{\mathrm b}\).

statements.statement: For \(G_{\mathrm b}\) and arbitrary normalized separable probes at both vertices, \(\operatorname{GID}_{\mathcal I}(Q_{z^{\circ},y})\) holds if and only if \(r_{z^{\circ}}\in\operatorname{row}(A_{\mathrm b})\) and \(e_y\in\operatorname{span}\{\phi_{Y_{\mathrm b},\beta_Y}:\beta_Y\in\mathcal L_{Y_{\mathrm b}}\}\). On success, any \(c\) satisfying \(c^{\mathsf T}A_{\mathrm b}=r_{z^{\circ}}^{\mathsf T}\) and any admissible effect-synthesis vector \(\mu^y\) give the synthesis- and coefficient-invariant functional \(Q_{z^{\circ},y}=\sum_{\beta_X\in\mathcal L_{X_{\mathrm b}}}c_{\beta_X}q^{\mathrm b}_{\beta_X}(y)\). If the treatment condition fails, an explicit treatment-null construction gives strictly positive same-evidence models with unequal queries; if the terminal condition fails, an explicit effect-null construction does so with singleton sources and primitive cell floor at least \(\min\{1/m,1/(2k)\}\).
statements.justification: This is the exact class-wide two-sided identification frontier for the smallest latent district.
statements.gap: Whole-mechanism recovery under marginal completeness does not give the latent bow's exact query criterion; here treatment row reachability and terminal effect reachability are separately necessary and jointly sufficient, with primitive-positive witnesses for either failure.
statements.consumer: Ananke obtains a complete constant-size oracle returning either an invariant functional or an executable positive twin certificate for the failed side.
statements.proof_tex:
Set
\[
 R_Y=\operatorname{span}\{\phi_{Y_{\mathrm b},\beta_Y}:\beta_Y\in\mathcal L_{Y_{\mathrm b}}\}.
\]
First suppose that \(r_{z^{\circ}}\in\operatorname{row}(A_{\mathrm b})\) and \(e_y\in R_Y\).  The first membership supplies a finite vector \(c\) such that
\[
 c^{\mathsf T}A_{\mathrm b}=r_{z^{\circ}}^{\mathsf T},
\]
and the second supplies an effect-synthesis vector \(\mu^y\) as in \texttt{def:terminal-synthesis}.  For every \(\mathcal M\in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{pp}}^{\mathrm{edge}}(G_{\mathrm b},\mathcal A)\), \texttt{lem:terminal-synthesis-invariance} gives
\[
 q^{\mathrm b}(y)=A_{\mathrm b}b_y,
 \qquad
 Q_{z^{\circ},y}(\mathcal M)=r_{z^{\circ}}^{\mathsf T}b_y,
\]
where \(b_y[a_{\mathrm b},z_{\mathrm b}]=B_{\mathcal M,y}(a_{\mathrm b},z_{\mathrm b})\).  Hence
\[
\begin{aligned}
 Q_{z^{\circ},y}(\mathcal M)
 &=c^{\mathsf T}A_{\mathrm b}b_y\\
 &=\sum_{\beta_X\in\mathcal L_{X_{\mathrm b}}}
 c_{\beta_X}q^{\mathrm b}_{\beta_X}(y).
\end{aligned}
\]
By \texttt{def:terminally-synthesized-bow-response}, the right-hand side is an explicit arithmetic functional of the accessible tensor.  Its value is independent of the admissible terminal synthesis by \texttt{lem:terminal-synthesis-invariance}, and independent of the admissible treatment coefficient by \texttt{lem:bow-coefficient-invariance}.  Consequently, equality of evidence implies equality of the causal query for every pair of models in the primitive-positive class, which is exactly \(\operatorname{GID}_{\mathcal I}(Q_{z^{\circ},y})\) by \texttt{def:global-probe-identification}.

For the converse, suppose first that \(r_{z^{\circ}}\notin\operatorname{row}(A_{\mathrm b})\).  Let \(R_X=\operatorname{row}(A_{\mathrm b})\).  Treatment-effect normalization and nonemptiness of each branch set imply that some treatment effect is nonzero; its paired state is a probability vector and hence nonzero, so \texttt{def:bow-probe-matrix} gives a nonzero row of \(A_{\mathrm b}\).  Thus \(R_X\ne\{0\}\).  Choose a matrix \(S_X\) whose columns form a basis of \(R_X\), and define
\[
 h=r_{z^{\circ}}-S_X(S_X^{\mathsf T}S_X)^{-1}S_X^{\mathsf T}r_{z^{\circ}}.
\]
Then \(h\perp R_X\), so \(A_{\mathrm b}h=0\); moreover \(h\ne0\) and
\[
 r_{z^{\circ}}^{\mathsf T}h=\lVert h\rVert_2^2>0.
\]
Thus the hypotheses of the already-established \texttt{lem:bow-positive-twins} hold.  That lemma produces \(\mathcal M_h^+,\mathcal M_h^-\) in the primitive-positive class with identical accessible evidence and unequal \(Q_{z^{\circ},y}\).  The implication in \texttt{def:global-probe-identification} therefore fails.

Suppose instead that \(e_y\notin R_Y\).  The proved \texttt{lem:bow-terminal-effect-positive-twins} produces two primitive-positive bow models with identical accessible evidence and query difference \(2t_\gamma\gamma(y)>0\).  Global identification again fails.  These two cases exhaust the failure of
\[
 r_{z^{\circ}}\in\operatorname{row}(A_{\mathrm b})
 \quad\text{and}\quad e_y\in R_Y.
\]
Together with sufficiency, they establish the exact two-sided criterion, the displayed invariant functional on success, and an explicit positive common-fiber obstruction on either kind of failure.

statements.statement: Suppose \(m=k=2\), every bow instrument is normalized, the terminal effects span \(\mathbb R^2\), and \(X_{\mathrm b}\) has one two-branch instrument whose two effects and two states are each linearly independent. Then \(r_0,r_1\notin\operatorname{row}(A_{\mathrm b})\). Both binary bow intervention responses fail global identification although the treatment instrument is marginally informationally complete in its separate effect and state margins.
statements.justification: The symbolic obstruction replaces the finite enumeration of minimal binary menus and remains valid under the exact weaker terminal condition.
statements.gap: Separate marginal completeness does not control the joint treatment row space in a latent bow; this proposition gives the smallest analytic counterexample class.
statements.consumer: This proposition supplies Ananke's smallest negative normalized-menu regression test under a terminal effect basis.
statements.proof_tex:
Write the two treatment-branch effects and states as columns \(\phi_0,\phi_1\in\mathbb R^2\) and \(\psi_0,\psi_1\in\mathbb R^2\).  By hypothesis, both pairs are linearly independent.  Normalization of the single two-branch treatment instrument gives
\[
 \phi_0+\phi_1=\mathbf 1.
\]
Under the standard identification of a vector in \(\mathbb R^4\) with a two-by-two matrix, \texttt{def:bow-probe-matrix} identifies the two rows of \(A_{\mathrm b}\) with \(\phi_0\psi_0^{\mathsf T}\) and \(\phi_1\psi_1^{\mathsf T}\), while \texttt{def:bow-target-coefficient} identifies \(r_z\) with \(\mathbf 1e_z^{\mathsf T}\), for \(z\in\{0,1\}\).

Suppose for contradiction that \(r_z\in\operatorname{row}(A_{\mathrm b})\).  Then there are scalars \(c_0,c_1\) such that
\[
 \mathbf 1e_z^{\mathsf T}
 =c_0\phi_0\psi_0^{\mathsf T}+c_1\phi_1\psi_1^{\mathsf T}
 =\Phi\begin{pmatrix}c_0&0\\0&c_1\end{pmatrix}\Psi^{\mathsf T},
 \qquad
 \Phi=(\phi_0\ \phi_1),\quad \Psi=(\psi_0\ \psi_1).
\]
Both \(\Phi\) and \(\Psi\) are invertible.  Thus the rank of the right-hand side is the number of nonzero elements of \(\{c_0,c_1\}\).  The left-hand side has rank one, so exactly one coefficient, say \(c_i\), is nonzero.  Equality of column spaces then forces \(\phi_i\) to be proportional to \(\mathbf 1\).  Since \(\phi_{1-i}=\mathbf 1-\phi_i\), the other effect is also proportional to \(\mathbf 1\), contradicting independence of \(\phi_0,\phi_1\).  Therefore
\[
 r_0,r_1\notin\operatorname{row}(A_{\mathrm b}).
\]

The independent treatment effects span \(\mathbb R^2\), as do the independent treatment states, so the treatment instrument is marginally informationally complete in both senses.  By the terminal-effect-span premise, \(e_y\) belongs to the span of the terminal effects for each binary outcome \(y\).  Applying \texttt{thm:bow-rowspan-iff} for \(z=0\) and \(z=1\), the failed treatment row-span condition implies failure of both corresponding global-identification predicates.  The terminal condition cannot repair the treatment-side obstruction.

statements.statement: For \(\mathcal I_{\mathrm b}^{\dagger}\), normalization holds for every instrument at both vertices, the treatment effect and state spans over \(\mathcal L_{X_{\mathrm b}}\) are both \(\mathbb R^2\), and the terminal effects \(e_0,e_1\) span \(\mathbb R^2\); indeed the matching terminal branches also satisfy \(e_0\otimes e_0=d_0\) and \(e_1\otimes e_1=d_1\). The treatment rows give \(\operatorname{rank}(A_{\mathrm b}^{\dagger})=3<4\), while \(r_0,r_1\in\operatorname{row}(A_{\mathrm b}^{\dagger})\). Hence both binary intervention-response distributions are globally identified on the latent bow although full treatment-table tomography is impossible. This is query-specific identification in a latent-confounded bow from a non-tomographic disturbing-probe menu.
statements.justification: The explicit menu separates query identification from both marginal completeness alone and four-dimensional treatment-table tomography under the exact terminal effect condition.
statements.gap: Whole-mechanism recovery on strictly positive Markovian DAG models does not imply this latent-source ADMG result; the bow recovers both intervention distributions from a rank-three treatment branch span plus a terminal effect basis.
statements.consumer: The four treatment rows and two terminal effect coordinates form Ananke's positive bow fixture adjacent to the minimal-menu failure fixture.

statements.statement: For the indexed tensor \(q_{\mathrm f}(x_{\mathrm f},y_{\mathrm f},b_{\mathrm f})\), applying \((K_{\mathrm f}^{\mathsf T})^{-1}=\begin{pmatrix}3/2&-1/2\\-1/2&3/2\end{pmatrix}\) to each \((x_{\mathrm f},y_{\mathrm f})\)-slice reconstructs \((P_{\mathrm f}(x_{\mathrm f},y_{\mathrm f},0),P_{\mathrm f}(x_{\mathrm f},y_{\mathrm f},1))=(42,6),(6,10),(10,6),(6,42)\) divided by \(128\), in \((x_{\mathrm f},y_{\mathrm f})=(0,0),(0,1),(1,0),(1,1)\) order. The ordinary front-door functional then equals \(3/8\) under \(\operatorname{do}(X_{\mathrm f}=0)\) and \(5/8\) under \(\operatorname{do}(X_{\mathrm f}=1)\).
statements.justification: The complete eight-cell table fixes the tensor ordering and checks that signed terminal inversion remains inside the probability simplex in this legal fixture.
statements.gap: Ordinary front-door identification starts from a passive law; this calculation reconstructs that law from explicitly indexed disturbing mediator-probe coordinates.
statements.consumer: The eight rational cells and two exact targets provide an end-to-end Ananke arithmetic test.
statements.proof_tex:
The determinant of \(K_{\mathrm f}^{\mathsf T}=K_{\mathrm f}\) is \(9/16-1/16=1/2\), so
\[
 (K_{\mathrm f}^{\mathsf T})^{-1}
 =\begin{pmatrix}3/2&-1/2\\-1/2&3/2\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Applying this matrix to the four slices from \texttt{def:frontdoor-instance} gives, in the stated order,
\[
\begin{aligned}
 (K_{\mathrm f}^{\mathsf T})^{-1}\binom{33}{15}&=\binom{42}{6},&
 (K_{\mathrm f}^{\mathsf T})^{-1}\binom{7}{9}&=\binom{6}{10},\\
 (K_{\mathrm f}^{\mathsf T})^{-1}\binom{9}{7}&=\binom{10}{6},&
 (K_{\mathrm f}^{\mathsf T})^{-1}\binom{15}{33}&=\binom{6}{42}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Every vector is divided by \(128\).  All eight reconstructed cells are strictly positive and their numerators sum to \(128\), so they define a joint probability mass \(P_{\mathrm f}\).  Its required marginals and conditionals are
\[
 P_{\mathrm f}(X_{\mathrm f}=0)=P_{\mathrm f}(X_{\mathrm f}=1)=\frac12,
\]
\[
\begin{array}{c|cc}
 &m_{\mathrm f}=0&m_{\mathrm f}=1\\ \hline
 P_{\mathrm f}(m_{\mathrm f}\mid X_{\mathrm f}=0)&3/4&1/4\\
 P_{\mathrm f}(m_{\mathrm f}\mid X_{\mathrm f}=1)&1/4&3/4
\end{array}
\]
and
\[
\begin{array}{c|cc}
 &m_{\mathrm f}=0&m_{\mathrm f}=1\\ \hline
 P_{\mathrm f}(Y_{\mathrm f}=1\mid X_{\mathrm f}=0,m_{\mathrm f})&1/8&5/8\\
 P_{\mathrm f}(Y_{\mathrm f}=1\mid X_{\mathrm f}=1,m_{\mathrm f})&3/8&7/8.
\end{array}
\]
Every denominator used here is positive by the displayed reconstructed table.

For completeness, the front-door equality can be derived directly from the independent-source semantics used in \texttt{lem:split-port-reduction}.  In \(G_{\mathrm f}\), let \(U\) denote the source on \(X_{\mathrm f}\leftrightarrow Y_{\mathrm f}\), and integrate the independent private sources into stochastic kernels \(\alpha(x\mid u)\), \(\mu(m\mid x)\), and \(\gamma(y\mid m,u)\).  The graph and \texttt{ass:independent-sources} give
\[
 P(x,m,y)=\sum_u p(u)\alpha(x\mid u)\mu(m\mid x)\gamma(y\mid m,u).
\]
There is no shared source between \(X_{\mathrm f}\) and \(M_{\mathrm f}\), so \(\mu(m\mid x)=P(m\mid x)\).  If
\[
 \pi_x(u)=\frac{p(u)\alpha(x\mid u)}{P(x)},
\]
then positivity gives
\[
 P(y\mid x,m)=\sum_u\pi_x(u)\gamma(y\mid m,u).
\]
Consequently,
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \sum_xP(x)P(y\mid x,m)
 &=\sum_{x,u}p(u)\alpha(x\mid u)\gamma(y\mid m,u)\\
 &=\sum_up(u)\gamma(y\mid m,u),
\end{aligned}
\]
because \(\sum_x\alpha(x\mid u)=1\).  Under \(\operatorname{do}(X_{\mathrm f}=x_0)\), the shared source retains its marginal \(p(u)\), the mediator is drawn from \(\mu(\cdot\mid x_0)\), and \(Y_{\mathrm f}\) has no direct \(X_{\mathrm f}\)-parent.  Finite marginalization therefore gives the ordinary front-door functional
\[
 P(Y_{\mathrm f}=y\mid\operatorname{do}(X_{\mathrm f}=x_0))
 =\sum_mP(m\mid x_0)\sum_xP(x)P(y\mid x,m).
\]
For \(y=1\), the inner sums at \(m=0\) and \(m=1\) are respectively
\[
 \frac12\frac18+\frac12\frac38=\frac14,
 \qquad
 \frac12\frac58+\frac12\frac78=\frac34.
\]
Thus
\[
\begin{aligned}
 P(Y_{\mathrm f}=1\mid\operatorname{do}(X_{\mathrm f}=0))
 &=\frac34\frac14+\frac14\frac34=\frac38,\\
 P(Y_{\mathrm f}=1\mid\operatorname{do}(X_{\mathrm f}=1))
 &=\frac14\frac14+\frac34\frac34=\frac58.
\end{aligned}
\]
This proves both the reconstruction and the two exact causal values.

statements.statement: Let \(w\) be fixable in \(\mathcal C\). If \(k_{\mathcal C}\) is a strictly positive normalized kernel on \(D\mathbin{\dot\cup}\{w\}\) given \(H\), then the coordinate formula \(\Phi_w(k_{\mathcal C})\) is strictly positive and satisfies \(N_D\Phi_w(k_{\mathcal C})=\mathbf 1\). Moreover the formula is exactly the ordinary one-step fixing quotient by the conditional mass of \(w\) given \(\operatorname{mb}_{\mathcal C}(w)\) and \(H\).
statements.justification: This proposition verifies the exact algebra performed before any causal lift is claimed.
statements.gap: Richardson et al. define fixing for a kernel already supplied by a passive law; this result isolates the coordinate quotient used for a probe-reconstructed candidate.
statements.consumer: Ananke can validate positivity and normalization of a proposed one-step certificate without invoking an SCM solver.
statements.proof_tex:
Put \(B=(\operatorname{mb}_{\mathcal C}(w)\cap D)\) and \(R=D\setminus B\).  Coordinates of fixed vertices that occur in the Markov blanket are already contained in \(a_H\).  Fix a context \((a_H,a_w)\).  For a value \(a_B\), the definitions of \(U_w\) and \(V_w\) give
\[
 u(a_w,a_B,a_H):=(U_wk_{\mathcal C})_{(a_w,a_B,a_H)}
   =\sum_{a_R}k_{\mathcal C}(a_R,a_B,a_w\mid a_H)
\]
and
\[
 v(a_B,a_H):=(V_wk_{\mathcal C})_{(a_B,a_H)}
   =\sum_{a'_w}\sum_{a_R}k_{\mathcal C}(a_R,a_B,a'_w\mid a_H)
   =\sum_{a'_w}u(a'_w,a_B,a_H).
\]
All alphabets are finite and nonempty.  Strict positivity of every cell of \(k_{\mathcal C}\) therefore implies \(u(a_w,a_B,a_H)>0\) and \(v(a_B,a_H)>0\), so every division in the definition of \(\Phi_w\) is valid.  That definition now yields, cell by cell,
\[
 \Phi_w(k_{\mathcal C})(a_R,a_B\mid a_H,a_w)
 =k_{\mathcal C}(a_R,a_B,a_w\mid a_H)
   \frac{v(a_B,a_H)}{u(a_w,a_B,a_H)}>0.
\]
For each fixed context \((a_H,a_w)\), finite summation and the two preceding identities give
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \sum_{a_D}\Phi_w(k_{\mathcal C})(a_D\mid a_H,a_w)
 &=\sum_{a_B}\frac{v(a_B,a_H)}{u(a_w,a_B,a_H)}
     \sum_{a_R}k_{\mathcal C}(a_R,a_B,a_w\mid a_H)\\
 &=\sum_{a_B}v(a_B,a_H)\\
 &=\sum_{a_B}\sum_{a'_w}\sum_{a_R}
     k_{\mathcal C}(a_R,a_B,a'_w\mid a_H)=1.
\end{aligned}
\]
The last equality is the assumed normalization of the kernel given \(H\).  By the definition of \(N_D\), these contextwise equalities are precisely \(N_D\Phi_w(k_{\mathcal C})=\mathbf 1\).

Finally,
\[
 \frac{u(a_w,a_B,a_H)}{v(a_B,a_H)}
 =k_{\mathcal C}(a_w\mid a_B,a_H)
 =k_{\mathcal C}\bigl(a_w\mid
   a_{\operatorname{mb}_{\mathcal C}(w)},a_H\bigr).
\]
Consequently \(\Phi_w(k_{\mathcal C})\) is exactly \(k_{\mathcal C}\) divided by the displayed conditional mass.  Assumption \(\text{ass:fixable-vertex}\) makes \(\phi_w(\mathcal C)\) a legal graphical fixing step; the positivity and normalization calculations themselves use only the displayed marginalizations and the positive normalized-kernel hypothesis.

statements.statement:
The universal shared-mechanism lift assertion is false for the displayed algebraic certificate.  In particular, take the empty ADMG on two binary random vertices \(w\) and \(d\), put \(D=\{d\}\) and \(H=\varnothing\), give each vertex one one-branch probe with \(\phi\equiv1\) and \(\psi(0)=\psi(1)=1/2\), take \(\Omega_D=\varnothing\), and choose the sole column of \(R_{\mathcal C}\) so that, at \(q^{\star}=1\),
\[
\begin{array}{c|cc}
k_{\mathcal C}(d,w)&w=0&w=1\\ \hline
d=0&2/5&1/10\\
d=1&1/10&2/5
\end{array}.
\]
Then \(q^{\star}\in\mathcal Q_{\mathcal I}\) and the coordinate fixing image \(\kappa_D=\Phi_w(k_{\mathcal C}(q^{\star}))\), given by
\[
\begin{array}{c|cc}
\kappa_D(d,w)&w=0&w=1\\ \hline
d=0&4/5&1/5\\
d=1&1/5&4/5
\end{array},
\]
belongs to \(\mathcal K_D^{\mathrm{alg}}(q^{\star})\), but it is not the one-step fixed district kernel of any \(\mathcal M'\in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{pp}}^{\mathrm{edge}}(G,\mathcal A)\), irrespective of a shared-mechanism requirement.  For the same binary empty graph, one-branch menu, and evidence \(q^{\star}=1\), a strictly positive normalized candidate kernel has a shared-mechanism lift if and only if it satisfies the additional equality
\[
 \kappa_D(0,0)=\kappa_D(0,1)
\]
is necessary and sufficient for a strictly positive lift.  It is the unique independent equality cutting the realizable kernels out of the two-dimensional space of normalized positive binary kernels given \(w\).  If its common value is \(p\in(0,1)\), a shared lift may be chosen with \(\mathcal M=\mathcal M'\), one state in each private-source alphabet, source-mass floor \(1\), and structural-kernel cell floor \(\min\{1/2,p,1-p\}>0\).
statements.proof_tex:
We verify every part of the counterexample.  Let \(V=\{w,d\}\), let both observed alphabets be \(\{0,1\}\), and let \(G\) have no directed or bidirected edges.  Thus \(\operatorname{dis}_{\mathcal C}(w)=\{w\}\) and \(\operatorname{de}_{\mathcal C}(w)=\{w\}\), so \(w\) satisfies \(\text{ass:fixable-vertex}\).  The one-branch effects satisfy instrument normalization because their sum is \(1\), and the stated \(\psi\)'s are full-support probability states.

First, \(q^{\star}=1\) is attainable.  For example, give each private source a singleton alphabet with mass \(1\), and set both parentless structural kernels equal to the Bernoulli \(1/2\) law.  This model has independent sources, source-mass floor \(1\), and mechanism-cell floor \(1/2\), hence belongs to \(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{pp}}^{\mathrm{edge}}(G,\mathcal A)\).  By the definitions of \(W_{\mathcal M}\) and \(\mathcal E_{\mathcal I}\), its sole accessible coordinate is
\[
\begin{aligned}
q^{\star}
&=\sum_{a,z}W_{\mathcal M}(a\mid z)
  \prod_{v\in\{w,d\}}1\cdot\frac12\\
&=\frac14\sum_z\sum_a W_{\mathcal M}(a\mid z)
=\frac14\sum_z1=1,
\end{aligned}
\]
because for every \(z\) the finite kernel \(W_{\mathcal M}(\cdot\mid z)\) is normalized and there are four binary values of \(z\).  The definition of \(\mathcal Q_{\mathcal I}\) therefore gives \(q^{\star}\in\mathcal Q_{\mathcal I}\).

Choose the four entries of the sole column of \(R_{\mathcal C}\) to be the displayed entries of \(k_{\mathcal C}\).  Since \(q^{\star}=1\), the definition of the reconstruction matrix gives exactly that table.  It is strictly positive and sums to \(1\).  Here \(\operatorname{mb}_{\mathcal C}(w)=\varnothing\), so the marginal matrices give
\[
(U_wk_{\mathcal C})(0)=(U_wk_{\mathcal C})(1)=\frac12,
\qquad V_wk_{\mathcal C}=1.
\]
The coordinate-fixing definition consequently gives
\[
\kappa_D(d,w)=\frac{k_{\mathcal C}(d,w)}{1/2}=2k_{\mathcal C}(d,w),
\]
which is the second displayed table.  Its entries are strictly positive and each column sums to \(1\), so \(N_D\kappa_D=\mathbf1\), also as guaranteed by \(\text{prop:one-fixing-coordinate-validity}\).  Because \(\Omega_D=\varnothing\), the equality \(O_D\kappa_D=S_Dq^{\star}\) has no rows and is vacuous.  Every defining condition of \(\mathcal K_D^{\mathrm{alg}}(q^{\star})\) is therefore satisfied.

It remains to prove non-realizability.  Consider any \(\mathcal M'\in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{pp}}^{\mathrm{edge}}(G,\mathcal A)\).  There are no edge sources, and the only sources \(U_w,U_d\) are private and independent.  With
\[
 \mu_w(x)=\sum_{u_w}p_w(u_w)f_w(x\mid u_w),
 \qquad
 \mu_d(x)=\sum_{u_d}p_d(u_d)f_d(x\mid u_d),
\]
the independent-source factorization and the empty graph give, equation by equation,
\[
\begin{aligned}
P_{\mathcal M'}(w=x,d=t)
&=\sum_{u_w,u_d}p_w(u_w)p_d(u_d)
 f_w(x\mid u_w)f_d(t\mid u_d)\\
&=\left(\sum_{u_w}p_w(u_w)f_w(x\mid u_w)\right)
  \left(\sum_{u_d}p_d(u_d)f_d(t\mid u_d)\right)\\
&=\mu_w(x)\mu_d(t).
\end{aligned}
\]
Strict source and mechanism positivity imply \(\mu_w(x)>0\) and \(\mu_d(t)>0\).  Ordinary fixing of \(w\), using the quotient proved in \(\text{prop:one-fixing-coordinate-validity}\), is therefore
\[
 \frac{P_{\mathcal M'}(w=x,d=t)}{P_{\mathcal M'}(w=x)}
 =\frac{\mu_w(x)\mu_d(t)}{\mu_w(x)}=\mu_d(t),
\]
which is independent of the fixed value \(x\).  Any realizable kernel must consequently satisfy \(\kappa_D(0,0)=\kappa_D(0,1)\).  The constructed certificate violates this equality because \(4/5\ne1/5\), so no \(\mathcal M'\) exists.  A fortiori there cannot be a pair \(\mathcal M,\mathcal M'\) having common observed-node tables and the other properties requested by the open question.

For completeness, we prove sufficiency and the asserted bounds in this instance.  Let \(\kappa_D\) be any strictly positive normalized binary kernel satisfying \(\kappa_D(0,0)=\kappa_D(0,1)=p\).  Column normalization gives \(\kappa_D(1,0)=\kappa_D(1,1)=1-p\), and strict positivity gives \(0<p<1\).  Give both private sources singleton alphabets of mass \(1\), set
\[
 f_d(0)=p,\qquad f_d(1)=1-p,
 \qquad f_w(0)=f_w(1)=\frac12,
\]
and take \(\mathcal M=\mathcal M'\).  The sources are independent, all source masses are at least \(1\), all mechanism cells are at least \(\min\{1/2,p,1-p\}>0\), and the same one-branch calculation gives accessible evidence \(q^{\star}=1\).  Fixing \(w\) yields \(f_d=\kappa_D\), so this is the required shared-mechanism lift.  Finally, a normalized binary kernel given binary \(w\) is parametrized by the two numbers \(\kappa_D(0,0)\) and \(\kappa_D(0,1)\); the realizable subset is cut out by their single equality.  Hence the equality is independent and minimal in this instance.
statements.justification: A positive normalized coordinate fixing image need not respect the ADMG's independent-source factorization; the theorem exhibits and exactly characterizes the first missing equality.
statements.gap: Ordinary fixing starts from a graph-compatible kernel, whereas the current algebraic certificate checks positivity, normalization, and selected overlaps but not all graph-implied equalities.
statements.consumer: Ananke must reject an algebraic one-step certificate until the relevant graph-specific equalities, including context invariance in the empty-graph case, have been checked.

statements.statement: For a normalized separable menu on \(G_{\mathrm b}\), if \(e_y\notin\operatorname{span}\{\phi_{Y_{\mathrm b},\beta_Y}:\beta_Y\in\mathcal L_{Y_{\mathrm b}}\}\), then there exist \(\mathcal M,\mathcal M'\in\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{pp}}^{\mathrm{edge}}(G_{\mathrm b},\mathcal A)\) with \(\mathcal E_{\mathcal I}(\mathcal M)=\mathcal E_{\mathcal I}(\mathcal M')\) and \(Q_{z^{\circ},y}(\mathcal M)\ne Q_{z^{\circ},y}(\mathcal M')\). They may be chosen with singleton exogenous alphabets, a common uniform treatment mechanism, and primitive cell floor at least \(\min\{1/m,1/(2k)\}\).
statements.proof_tex:
Let
\[
 R_Y=\operatorname{span}\{\phi_{Y_{\mathrm b},\beta_Y}:\beta_Y\in\mathcal L_{Y_{\mathrm b}}\}
 \subseteq\mathbb R^{\mathcal A_{Y_{\mathrm b}}},
\]
and suppose \(e_y\notin R_Y\).  Fix any terminal instrument label \(j_Y\).  By \texttt{ass:instrument-normalization},
\[
 \mathbf 1=\sum_{b_Y\in\mathcal B_{Y_{\mathrm b},j_Y}}
 \phi_{Y_{\mathrm b},(j_Y,b_Y)}\in R_Y.
\]
In particular, \(R_Y\) is nonzero.  Choose a matrix \(S\) whose columns form a basis of \(R_Y\).  The columns are linearly independent, so \(S^{\mathsf T}S\) is positive definite and invertible.  Put
\[
 \gamma=e_y-S(S^{\mathsf T}S)^{-1}S^{\mathsf T}e_y.
\]
Then \(\gamma\perp R_Y\), and \(\gamma\ne0\) because \(e_y\notin R_Y\).  Writing \(e_y=S\alpha+\gamma\), where \(S\alpha\perp\gamma\), gives
\[
 \gamma(y)=e_y^{\mathsf T}\gamma=\lVert\gamma\rVert_2^2>0.
\]
Since \(\mathbf 1\in R_Y\) and \(\gamma\perp R_Y\), it follows that
\[
 \sum_{a_{\mathrm t}\in\mathcal A_{Y_{\mathrm b}}}\gamma(a_{\mathrm t})=0.
\]
Let \(L_\gamma=\lVert\gamma\rVert_\infty>0\) and \(t_\gamma=1/(2kL_\gamma)>0\).  For \(\sigma\in\{+1,-1\}\), construct \(\mathcal N^\sigma\) on \(G_{\mathrm b}\) as follows.  Give every private and bidirected-edge source a singleton alphabet with mass one; these masses are strictly positive and factor independently.  Set
\[
 f_{X_{\mathrm b}}^\sigma(a_{\mathrm b}\mid u)=\frac1m,
 \qquad
 f_{Y_{\mathrm b}}^\sigma(a_{\mathrm t}\mid z_{\mathrm b},u)
 =\frac1k+\sigma t_\gamma\gamma(a_{\mathrm t}).
\]
The displayed terminal kernel ignores its allowed parent and source arguments, which is permitted by the bow graph.  Its cells sum to one because \(\sum_{a_{\mathrm t}}\gamma(a_{\mathrm t})=0\), and
\[
 f_{Y_{\mathrm b}}^\sigma(a_{\mathrm t}\mid z_{\mathrm b},u)
 \ge \frac1k-t_\gamma L_\gamma=\frac1{2k}>0.
\]
The treatment cells equal \(1/m>0\).  Thus \texttt{ass:independent-sources}, \texttt{ass:strict-source-positivity}, \texttt{ass:strict-mechanism-positivity}, and \texttt{def:primitive-positive-edge-scm-class} imply
\[
 \mathcal N^+,\mathcal N^-\in
 \mathfrak M_{\mathrm{pp}}^{\mathrm{edge}}(G_{\mathrm b},\mathcal A),
\]
with primitive cell floor at least \(\min\{1/m,1/(2k)\}\).

The split-port kernel is explicitly
\[
 W_{\mathcal N^\sigma}((a_{\mathrm b},a_{\mathrm t})\mid
 (z_{\mathrm b},z_{\mathrm t}))
 =\frac1m\left(\frac1k+\sigma t_\gamma\gamma(a_{\mathrm t})\right).
\]
For any accessible branch pair, \texttt{def:probe-evidence-map} and finite factorization of the sums give
\[
\begin{aligned}
 &\bar q^{+}_{\beta_X,\beta_Y}-\bar q^{-}_{\beta_X,\beta_Y}\\
 &\quad=\frac{2t_\gamma}{m}
 \left(\sum_{a_{\mathrm b},z_{\mathrm b}}
 \phi_{X_{\mathrm b},\beta_X}(a_{\mathrm b})
 \psi_{X_{\mathrm b},\beta_X}(z_{\mathrm b})\right)
 \left(\sum_{a_{\mathrm t},z_{\mathrm t}}
 \phi_{Y_{\mathrm b},\beta_Y}(a_{\mathrm t})
 \psi_{Y_{\mathrm b},\beta_Y}(z_{\mathrm t})
 \gamma(a_{\mathrm t})\right)\\
 &\quad=\frac{2t_\gamma}{m}
 \left(\sum_{a_{\mathrm b},z_{\mathrm b}}
 \phi_{X_{\mathrm b},\beta_X}(a_{\mathrm b})
 \psi_{X_{\mathrm b},\beta_X}(z_{\mathrm b})\right)
 \left(\sum_{a_{\mathrm t}}
 \phi_{Y_{\mathrm b},\beta_Y}(a_{\mathrm t})\gamma(a_{\mathrm t})\right)
 =0.
\end{aligned}
\]
Here \(\sum_{z_{\mathrm t}}\psi_{Y_{\mathrm b},\beta_Y}(z_{\mathrm t})=1\), and the last inner product vanishes because \(\gamma\perp R_Y\).  Hence every coordinate agrees and
\[
 \mathcal E_{\mathcal I}(\mathcal N^+)=\mathcal E_{\mathcal I}(\mathcal N^-).
\]
On the other hand, \texttt{def:atomic-query-contraction} gives
\[
 Q_{z^{\circ},y}(\mathcal N^\sigma)
 =\sum_{a_{\mathrm b}}\frac1m
 \left(\frac1k+\sigma t_\gamma\gamma(y)\right)
 =\frac1k+\sigma t_\gamma\gamma(y),
\]
and therefore
\[
 Q_{z^{\circ},y}(\mathcal N^+)-Q_{z^{\circ},y}(\mathcal N^-)
 =2t_\gamma\gamma(y)>0.
\]
These are the required strictly positive same-evidence twins.

statements.statement:
Let \(m=2\).  For every normalized binary separable probe menu \(\mathcal I\)
on \(G_{\mathrm b}\) whose treatment effects satisfy
\(\operatorname{span}\{\phi_{X_{\mathrm b},\beta_X}:\beta_X\in
\mathcal L_{X_{\mathrm b}}\}=\mathbb R^2\), if
\(r_0,r_1\in\operatorname{row}(A_{\mathrm b})\), then
\(\operatorname{rank}(A_{\mathrm b})\geq 3\), and hence
\(\lvert\mathcal L_{X_{\mathrm b}}\rvert\geq3\).  The explicit menu
\(\mathcal I_{\mathrm b}^{\dagger}\) has marginally complete treatment
effects, contains both \(r_0\) and \(r_1\) in
\(\operatorname{row}(A_{\mathrm b}^{\dagger})\), and satisfies
\(\operatorname{rank}(A_{\mathrm b}^{\dagger})=3\).  Thus three is the exact
minimum attainable treatment branch-matrix rank among normalized marginally
effect-complete binary menus containing both bow target rows.  This is a
minimum-rank attainment statement, not a claim that every rank-three menu
contains the target rows.
statements.proof_tex:
For the lower bound, set
\[
  S=\operatorname{span}\{r_0,r_1\}
   =\{\mathbf 1\otimes w:w\in\mathbb R^2\}.
\]
The second equality follows from \texttt{def:bow-target-coefficient}, since
\(r_0=\mathbf 1\otimes e_0\) and
\(r_1=\mathbf 1\otimes e_1\), and \(e_0,e_1\) are the coordinate basis of
\(\mathbb R^2\).  In particular, \(\dim(S)=2\).  If both target rows belong
to \(\operatorname{row}(A_{\mathrm b})\), then
\(S\subseteq\operatorname{row}(A_{\mathrm b})\), so
\(\operatorname{rank}(A_{\mathrm b})\geq2\).

Suppose, for contradiction, that
\(\operatorname{rank}(A_{\mathrm b})<3\).  The preceding lower bound forces
\(\operatorname{rank}(A_{\mathrm b})=2\), whence
\[
  \operatorname{row}(A_{\mathrm b})=S.
\]
For every tagged treatment branch \(\beta_X\),
\texttt{def:bow-probe-matrix} says that its row, viewed as a two-by-two matrix,
is
\[
  \phi_{X_{\mathrm b},\beta_X}
  \psi_{X_{\mathrm b},\beta_X}^{\mathsf T}.
\]
Membership of this row in \(S\) says that its two matrix rows are equal.
Writing \(\phi_{X_{\mathrm b},\beta_X}=(\phi(0),\phi(1))^{\mathsf T}\), this
equality is
\[
  (\phi(0)-\phi(1))
  \psi_{X_{\mathrm b},\beta_X}^{\mathsf T}=0.
\]
Every \(\psi_{X_{\mathrm b},\beta_X}\) is a probability vector and therefore
is nonzero.  It follows that \(\phi(0)=\phi(1)\), so every treatment effect is
proportional to \(\mathbf 1\), including the possible zero effect.  Their
span is therefore contained in the one-dimensional space
\(\operatorname{span}\{\mathbf 1\}\), contradicting the stated marginal
effect completeness.  Thus
\(\operatorname{rank}(A_{\mathrm b})\geq3\).  Since matrix rank cannot exceed
the number of rows, the number of tagged treatment branches is at least
three.

It remains to prove attainment from the frozen construction, rather than
assuming it.  By \texttt{def:binary-bow-menu}, the treatment rows of
\(A_{\mathrm b}^{\dagger}\) are
\[
 u^{+}=\mathbf 1\otimes\psi^{+},\qquad
 u^{-}=\mathbf 1\otimes\psi^{-},\qquad
 v_0=e_0\otimes\psi^{+},\qquad
 v_1=e_1\otimes\psi^{+},
\]
where
\(\psi^{+}=(3/4,1/4)^{\mathsf T}\) and
\(\psi^{-}=(1/4,3/4)^{\mathsf T}\).  The one-branch instruments have effect
\(\mathbf 1\), while the two-branch instrument has effects \(e_0,e_1\).
Therefore their branchwise effect sums equal \(\mathbf 1\), as required by
\texttt{ass:instrument-normalization}, and the displayed effect family spans
\(\mathbb R^2\).

Because \(u^{+}=v_0+v_1\), the four rows have rank at most three.  On the
other hand, \(v_0,v_1,u^{-}\) are linearly independent.  Indeed, if
\(\alpha v_0+\beta v_1+\gamma u^{-}=0\), its two matrix rows give
\[
  \alpha\psi^{+}+\gamma\psi^{-}=0,
  \qquad
  \beta\psi^{+}+\gamma\psi^{-}=0.
\]
The determinant of the matrix with columns \(\psi^{+},\psi^{-}\) is
\(9/16-1/16=1/2\), so those states are linearly independent.  The first
equation yields \(\alpha=\gamma=0\), and the second then yields \(\beta=0\).
Consequently
\(\operatorname{rank}(A_{\mathrm b}^{\dagger})=3\).

Finally, direct arithmetic gives
\[
 e_0=\frac32\psi^{+}-\frac12\psi^{-},\qquad
 e_1=-\frac12\psi^{+}+\frac32\psi^{-}.
\]
Tensoring these equalities on the left by \(\mathbf 1\) yields
\[
 r_0=\frac32u^{+}-\frac12u^{-},\qquad
 r_1=-\frac12u^{+}+\frac32u^{-}.
\]
Thus both target rows belong to
\(\operatorname{row}(A_{\mathrm b}^{\dagger})\).  The universal lower bound
and this explicit rank-three witness together prove that the minimum
attainable rank under the stated conditions is exactly three.

statements.statement:
Let \(m=2\).  For every normalized separable probe menu \(\mathcal I\) on
\(G_{\mathrm b}\), suppose that
\(\operatorname{span}\{\phi_{X_{\mathrm b},\beta_X}:\beta_X\in
\mathcal L_{X_{\mathrm b}}\}=\mathbb R^2\) and that
\(r_0,r_1\in\operatorname{row}(A_{\mathrm b})\).  Then
\(\operatorname{rank}(A_{\mathrm b})\ge3\), and consequently
\(\lvert\mathcal L_{X_{\mathrm b}}\rvert\ge3\).

Among normalized binary separable menus on \(G_{\mathrm b}\) whose treatment
effect and state spans are both \(\mathbb R^2\), whose terminal effects span
\(\mathbb R^2\), and for which
\(\operatorname{GID}_{\mathcal I}(Q_{z^{\circ},y})\) holds for every
\(z^{\circ},y\in\{0,1\}\) on
\(\mathfrak M_{\mathrm{pp}}^{\mathrm{edge}}(G_{\mathrm b},\mathcal A)\),
the minimum possible value of \(\operatorname{rank}(A_{\mathrm b})\) is
three.  The minimum is attained by \(\mathcal I_{\mathrm b}^{\dagger}\),
whose treatment menu is one three-branch instrument.  This is a universal
lower bound together with an attaining menu, not a claim that every
rank-three menu identifies the queries.

sampling_model.design: A fixed finite menu of known separable local probe kernels, with branch effects normalized separately within each instrument label.
sampling_model.units: The proposal's identification claims concern exact accessible regime probabilities; empirical sampling is outside the frozen bow and one-fixing scope.
sampling_model.treatment: The causal target is \(\operatorname{do}(X=x)\), which need not coincide with an accessible probe regime.
sampling_model.overlap: Every primitive source mass and every structural-kernel cell is strictly positive, a condition stronger than positivity of the induced observed law.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The local probe states and effects are known; no nuisance estimator is introduced in this discovery core.

estimand_functional: \(\operatorname{GID}_{\mathcal I}(Q_{z^{\circ},y})\Longleftrightarrow[r_{z^{\circ}}\in\operatorname{row}(A_{\mathrm b})\text{ and }e_y\in\operatorname{span}\{\phi_{Y_{\mathrm b},\beta_Y}:\beta_Y\in\mathcal L_{Y_{\mathrm b}}\}]\); when both conditions hold, \(Q_{z^{\circ},y}=\sum_{\beta_X\in\mathcal L_{X_{\mathrm b}}}c_{\beta_X}q^{\mathrm b}_{\beta_X}(y)\) for any \(c^{\mathsf T}A_{\mathrm b}=r_{z^{\circ}}^{\mathsf T}\) and any admissible effect synthesis \(\mu^y\)

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Definitions 8--9 and Proposition 6 formulate separate marginal effect and state completeness, and Theorem 1 recovers whole mechanisms for strictly positive Markovian causal models on DAGs.
Sections 2--4 define legal fixing and intrinsic kernels starting from a supplied passive-law kernel.
The ID algorithm is sound and complete for passive observational input, with a hedge witnessing nonidentification.
General identifiability under observed-law positivity requires positivity-aware failure constructions.
Finite discrete causal compatibility can be encoded as polynomial optimization over canonical response functions.
The front-door criterion identifies an intervention distribution from a compatible passive observed law.

tldr: Known disturbing probes reveal contractions of both input and output ports, not a passive observed law. On the primitive-positive canonical edge-source bow with joint terminal target-span, global identification is exactly a treatment-branch row-span condition: success yields a terminal-synthesis- and coefficient-invariant arithmetic functional, while failure yields strictly positive same-evidence twins through an explicit invertible \(m^2\)-coordinate operator and an \(m\)-state shared source. An explicit marginally complete three-instrument menu has only a three-dimensional treatment branch span, has matching terminal input-output branches, and identifies both bow responses, giving a query-identification result in a latent-confounded regime distinct from Markovian mechanism recovery. Beyond the bow, the scope stops after one legal CADMG fixing step: every reconstruction, conditional quotient, normalization row, and retained overlap is written as a finite matrix contract, and the genuinely causal independent-edge-source lift from the strictly positive algebraic certificate is exposed as the open question.

project_justification.gap: Friend et al. recover mechanisms from marginally complete disturbing instruments in the Markovian regime, while ordinary ADMG fixing starts from an already valid passive-law kernel. Neither addresses the distinct problem of query identification on a latent bow or shows that a positive normalized array reconstructed from disturbing-probe coordinates is induced by independent per-edge sources.
project_justification.niche: Within the primitive-positive latent-bow regime, the project identifies the query-specific row-span frontier between marginal completeness alone and full split-port tomography, and at the first legal fixing step isolates a precise algebraic-versus-causal realizability gap.
project_justification.fill: The project proves the exact bow row-span equivalence under an explicit joint terminal target-span condition, invariant synthesis, dimensionally explicit bounded positive twins, and the non-tomographic positive menu; it then isolates one coordinate-level fixing certificate and the shared-mechanism edge-source lift as the sole open construction.

related_work: Friend, Kissinger, Spekkens, and Wolfe (2025, Definitions 8--9, Proposition 6, and Theorem 1) formalize separable disturbing instruments and recover Markovian mechanisms under marginal informational completeness. The present binary-bow theorem studies a different latent-confounded graph and query target, using that instrument framework as motivation: both bow intervention responses are recovered from a three-dimensional branch span although full four-dimensional branch-map tomography fails; no theorem-class containment or tightening of Friend et al. is claimed. Richardson, Evans, Robins, and Shpitser (2023, Sections 2--4) define fixability and kernel fixing when a passive-law kernel is already available; the coordinate proposition reduces exactly to their one-step quotient, whereas causal realization of a probe-reconstructed algebraic certificate is left open. Shpitser and Pearl (2006, Theorems 1--2) inform the common-fiber witness benchmark, and Kivva et al. (2022) inform the insistence on positive failure constructions; neither is claimed to establish primitive-positive disturbing-probe twins. Duarte et al. (2024) and Zhang, Tian, and Bareinboim (2022) inform finite response-type and support-reduction techniques, but they do not supply shared observed mechanisms with mutually independent per-bidirected-edge sources. Pearl (1995) supplies the ordinary front-door endpoint checked by the explicit eight-cell reconstruction. Full branch-map tomography is treated only as standard finite-dimensional boundary infrastructure.
technical_internal_limitation: The equalities defining the algebraic set use only finite vectors and matrices. Positivity, normalization, and all listed overlaps do not by themselves certify membership in the canonical independent-edge-source SCM class. The source-product and shared-mechanism lift is therefore not asserted by the certificate or by the coordinate fixing proposition.
honest_scope: The finite claims are the bow row-span equivalence under joint terminal target-span, its two independent dual-invariance lemmas, the typed positive-twin cancellation identity, the explicit positive twins, the minimal-menu obstruction, the three-instrument query separation, the rational front-door check, and positivity and normalization of one coordinate fixing quotient. The matching binary terminal branches reduce exactly to \(e_0\otimes e_0=d_0\) and \(e_1\otimes e_1=d_1\); the front-door fixture reduces to the eight cells \((42,6;6,10;10,6;6,42)/128\) and targets \(3/8,5/8\). The shared-mechanism independent-edge-source lift from the algebraic one-step certificate, including a finite latent-support bound or a smallest extra algebraic obstruction, is open. No all-ADMG recursive calculus, complexity theorem, or inference theorem is claimed. Under passive observation, the coordinate map reduces to the ordinary one-step fixing quotient; under a full branch span, standard tomography remains a boundary case rather than a contribution.
